first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (activation down 6% QoQ, onboarding completion down 4% QoQ) map directly onto the mechanism documented in memory_31 and memory_86, both of which report durable, clean lifts in SMB activation/completion from onboarding simplification with no noted downside to revenue quality. This is the most direct, evidence-backed lever for the metrics actually deteriorating right now. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but reacting in-kind risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts that erode long-term qualified revenue rather than protect it — a discount war is not clearly the sustainable play, and that memory doesn't speak to long-term retention/margin quality. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) and referral incentives (memory_57) don't address the acute, dropping metrics this week. With only one experiment slot, I verify the two memories most load-bearing for the chosen action to confirm the original effect sizes and conditions still look sound before committing capacity, and keep scale at a standard (not broad) experiment since this is a rerun of a previously validated lever rather than a novel bet, while still respecting that current-quarter dynamics (competitor pressure) could interact with onboarding changes in ways prior data didn't capture.

final.rationale: Archive confirms both source records: exp_31 (signup simplification) shows activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, but a small -1% dip in 30-day retention, and explicitly notes it holds on SMB only, not replicated elsewhere. exp_86 (shortened onboarding) confirms completion +13%, time-to-value improved, and retention +3% — a cleaner, stronger result with no noted downside. Together these directly target the two metrics currently declining (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) and are the best-evidenced lever available this week, especially compared to reactive promotional pricing which risks pulling in low-quality, price-sensitive accounts amid a competitor price war — a move that could win short-term signups at the cost of sustainable qualified revenue. I still flag downstream_value_risk because exp_31's -1% retention dip, even if small and outweighed by revenue gain, means the combined onboarding-simplification lever isn't unambiguously clean, and its confirmed scope is SMB-only, not general. Given that, I keep the experiment at standard scale rather than broad rollout, targeting the SMB self-serve segment where the effect is confirmed, so we capture the likely benefit on the metrics under pressure without over-committing this week's single slot to an unreplicated broader claim. This preserves the option to reassess promotional response or enterprise-assist plays in future weeks once this week's result and competitive dynamics are clearer.
